clue.text: Could make both meteor and woman pregnant

indicators.note: the letters of these two words could be reshaped to make something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange claim that some agent could leave both a falling star and a woman with child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could make' is the anagram signal: the letters of BOTH METEOR rearrange to give the answer; 'and' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant mother is a woman who is pregnant, described by the hyphenated phrase for someone about to become a parent.

clue.text: Brand new herb

explanation.definitionFit: Mint describes something in perfect, unused condition, and it is also the familiar aromatic plant used in cooking.

clue.text: Musical figure featured by Mott the Hoople

definitions.text: Musical figure featured by Mott the Hoople

parts.words: Musical figure featured by Mott the Hoople
parts.note: the band's name, written out, has three Ts in a row across its first two words, a little group of three

explanation.surface: A music critic noting a passage that the 1970s glam-rock band Mott the Hoople made a feature of.
explanation.walkthrough: Mott the Hoople was a British glam-rock band. Run MOTT and THE together and three Ts stand side by side: a group of three notes, as it were, sits in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a group of three notes played in the time of two is called by this word, which also names any set of three.

clue.text: Why I cry? We have corruption all over the place

indicators.note: corruption spoils or distorts something, so the letters before it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting their tears because they live amid corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruption' is the anagram signal; 'have' looks like a linking verb but belongs to the letters that are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in all directions or in total disorder, the same scattered sense as chaotic spread.

clue.text: Walks poorly-rated by Sun

indicators.note: done poorly, the word rated comes out of order and is rearranged

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A review of strolls given a low mark by the Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'poorly-rated' disguises the split: 'poorly' alone is the anagram signal, and 'by' merely places Sunday's abbreviation alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to step or walk, so the third-person verb form matches the plural noun-looking clue word.

clue.text: Was appropriate to be almost more athletic in bed

indicators.note: in places the shortened word within the letters of bed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: fitter means in better physical shape

explanation.surface: Is it fitting to be a little sportier in the bedroom?
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' docks the comparative's last letter, and 'in' lodges what is left inside the bed; 'to' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit something is to suit it, so having befitted means having been suitable or proper for it.

clue.text: Frightening cut to cause permanent damage

indicators.note: cut here means the word is docked of its last letter

parts.note: scary means frightening

explanation.surface: A horror-film wound that leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a noun for a wound, but it is a deletion signal that docks the final Y from SCARY; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To scar someone is to mark or harm them lastingly, physically or emotionally.

clue.text: Instrument online in case accountant comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the accountant's letters surround what is placed in the middle

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
E, as in e-mail or e-commerce, marks something online
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: An online instrument is being investigated when an auditor visits the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' wraps C and A around E plus LEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, giving a bell-like sound.

clue.text: Primed for action, gunners surround country

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
a ring is something that encircles
Togo is a West African country

explanation.surface: Artillery troops ready to encircle a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be eager and ready to start is the idiom's sense, matching prepared for action.

clue.text: North American doctor that's preserving innocence

indicators.note: preserving means holding inside, so the doctor sits within the letters for that's

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor from North America who keeps his innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for i.e., which 'preserving' wraps around VET.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of worldly experience, a guileless simplicity close to innocence.

clue.text: Artist gets in line with resistance weaker

indicators.note: gets in means the artist goes inside the line

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A painter joins a queue alongside a weakened resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' places the Royal Academician inside a queue; 'resistance' is the physics symbol, not a wartime underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailer is the comparative of frail, meaning more feeble or less strong.

clue.text: Pale pipe suggests neatness

parts.note: put the letters of the first two words of the answer in a new order and they spell these two clue words

explanation.surface: A pale smoking pipe hints at tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rearrange APPLE PIE and you get PALE PIPE, the clue's opening words. 'suggests' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in this state is perfectly arranged, so the phrase stands for neatness and good order.

clue.text: Made a lot of something pie-lady put out

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of their order and reshuffled

explanation.surface: A pie-seller sets something out and makes a fuss about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on PIELADY plus PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate or emphasise something is to make much of it, which is what this phrase says.

clue.text: See 23
What I did with exam after bear persists

indicators.note: after means the exam phrase follows the word for bear

parts.note: to stick something is to bear or tolerate it
a candidate who took an exam sat it

explanation.surface: A student explains that the exam came straight after a bear encounter, and still keeps at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is a verb, not the animal: to stick it is to tolerate it.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going doggedly at a task is to persevere, which the idiom expresses.

clue.text: Irritable gut, etc, hypodermically controlled

indicators.note: controlled here means held within, so the answer is contained in the run of words

explanation.surface: A medical note on an upset stomach treated by injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlled' signals that the answer is held inside gu-T ETC HY-podermically.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means easily annoyed, short-tempered.

clue.text: Ghost never returns a book

indicators.note: returns means the word never is read backwards

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A ghost who never gives back a borrowed book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns NEVER into REVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A revenant is one who comes back from the dead, a spectre.

clue.text: Police track beginning with a guitar effect

parts.note: the fuzz is slang for the police

indicators.note: beginning means only the first letter of track is used

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A police recording that opens with a guitar effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes the T of 'track'; 'with' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuzz tone is a deliberately distorted electric-guitar sound produced by a pedal or amplifier.

clue.text: Member of pack cut without degree at Open University

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word cut goes round the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree
OU is the Open University, a UK distance-learning university

explanation.surface: Someone dropped from the team for lacking a degree from the Open University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so the word cut wraps round the degree and the university.
explanation.definitionFit: Young Scouts are organised in packs, so a junior Scout is a member of a pack.

clue.text: Drained, sore internally having fought

indicators.note: internally means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: bled means drained, as of blood or money
raw means sore, as skin can be

explanation.surface: An exhausted, aching boxer after a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drained, sore' reads like a description of the fighter, but each word is a piece, and 'internally' sets the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To brawl is to fight in a rough, noisy way, so the past tense means fought.

clue.text: Musk, perhaps one worn by the Prince Regent

definitions.meaning: an important person, and the tycoon Elon Musk is one example

definitions.text: one worn by the Prince Regent
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a ..., the fashionable headwear of the Regency era

explanation.surface: Imagining a billionaire wearing a Regency-era wig.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince Regent ruled Britain for his father George III from 1811 to 1820, when gentlemen still wore large wigs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an important or influential person, and literally a large wig like those worn by eighteenth-century grandees.

clue.text: Show how to change reference book

indicators.note: to change means the letters of the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to update a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' is the anagram signal on SHOWHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an annual biographical dictionary of notable people, a standard reference work.

clue.text: Concert percussionist drawn on time

parts.note: a Prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

indicators.note: drawn means disembowelled, the insides removed, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A drummer at a concert sketched in time with the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' looks like sketched, but means gutted as in hanged, drawn and quartered: only P and T of 'percussionist' remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means punctual, arriving or acting exactly when expected.

clue.text: Salt spring?

definitions.meaning: to ... food is to add salt or other flavouring
spring is one example of a ... of the year, hence the question mark

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for flavouring food and the name for a quarter of the year such as spring.

clue.text: Character with antelope from Australia

parts.note: the izard is a goat-antelope of the Pyrenees, a kind of chamois
of means from, as in a man of Kent
Oz is slang for Australia

explanation.surface: A person who arrives with an antelope from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is the whole definition; the izard is an obscure animal well known to crossword setters.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of L. Frank Baum's story is a fictional character, the humbug ruler of the Emerald City.

clue.text: Greek dish of stodgy roulade

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the answer comes from inside the following words

explanation.surface: Choosing between a Greek meal and a heavy rolled dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points to the letters inside stod-GY RO-ulade.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyro is Greek meat cooked on a vertical spit and served in pitta, a variant name for gyros.

clue.text: Fox over there at Holly roundabout

indicators.note: roundabout means going round in circles, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A huntsman spots a fox on the far side of the Holly road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' is the anagram signal, not a traffic circle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cry a hunter gives on sighting the quarry, announcing that a fox is in view.

clue.text: Mother went off course, reflected and stepped aside

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: reflected means turned as in a mirror, so the word for veering is read backwards

parts.note: yawed means swung off course, as a ship or plane does

explanation.surface: A mother takes a wrong turn, thinks it over and gets out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' looks like thought, but it turns YAWED back to DEWAY; 'and' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To make way is to move aside so that someone else can pass.

clue.text: Note about unconscious trend

indicators.note: about means going around, so the note's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the id is the unconscious part of the psyche in Freud's theory

explanation.surface: A memo concerning an unconscious tendency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconscious' is Freud's id, not the state of being knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide of opinion is a general drift or tendency, so the word can stand for a trend.

clue.text: Having more money a wiser course of action

definitions.meaning: the hyphenated comparative of well-to-do, meaning more prosperous
read as a phrase, it is preferable to do something

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is wealthier, the comparative of well-off; the other is the phrase saying an action is preferable.
